messages:
maria: Nightly perf alert: p50 +12%, p95 +28%, throughput -18% on prod-cluster-3 since 02:00 UTC. Spike aligns with merge PR#5124. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/xyz

deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary=2026-03-17T01:58Z, rollout step=5/8

kai: saw the alert. assigning triage. @sophie @nate can you take a quick look at kernel selection + KV metrics?

sophie: looking. PR touched batching/window tunables and prefetch hint heuristics. CI perf run had a 4% tail increase but passed.

nate: starting quick profiler run on canary nodes. grabbing top stacks.

sophie: profiler snapshot (summary): 
```
hot paths:
- kv::evict (increased 2.8x)
- batch::coalesce
- kernel_selector::fallback_check
kv_hit_rate=0.67 -> down from 0.92 pre-PR
```

kai: interesting — kv_hit_rate drop could force different kernel choice. any change to kernel_freq thresholds in PR?

sophie: no kernel changes. but batching.window extended from 12ms -> 25ms; prefetch now issues earlier hints for predicted contexts. hypothesize: longer batching + aggressive prefetch -> larger active set thrash -> kv eviction -> more fallback kernels -> tail latency.

maria: can we bisect? simplest is revert batching.window change on canary.

nate: reverting PR-5124 on canary now.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: canary=rollback-PR5124 @ 03:12Z

maria: rolling hold on global rollout. step paused.

kai: metrics update — 10m after rollback p95 back near baseline, throughput recovering. looks like rollback fixed it.

sophie: dug into kernel_selector logs: when kv_hit_rate<0.8 selector prefers conservative kernel path which increases per-token latency by ~25% for long contexts. coupling effect with larger batch window amplified tail.

nate: created temporary guard: if kv_eviction_rate > 0.2 don't extend batching.window beyond 15ms. patch applied to canary agent.

maria: nice. next steps?

sophie: open follow-up:
- revert PR fully from release branch until fix merged
- add CI perf test that simulates KV hotset churn
- adjust selector to consider recent KV hit-rate histogram rather than single threshold
- add telemetry for prefetch -> evict correlation

kai: filing release-blocker and scheduling quick postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT. @eng-runtime-oncall add to rotation notes.

eng-runtime-oncall: added. thanks.

maria: thanks everyone — good catch. we'll keep the rollout paused until root-cause PR lands.
